'''Mohammad Khaja Nazeeruddin''' (born 1957 in Thumboor, Andhra Pradesh, India) is an [[Indians in Switzerland|Indian-Swiss]] [[chemist]] and [[Materials science|materials scientist]] who conducts research on  [[Perovskite solar cell]]s, dye-sensitized solar cells, and light-emitting diodes. He is a professor at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]] (École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne) and the director of the Laboratory for [[Molecular engineering|Molecular Engineering]] of Functional Materials at School of Basic Sciences.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=GMF|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/gmf/|access-date=2020-12-21|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Prof. Nazeeruddin|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/gmf/nazeeruddin/|access-date=2020-12-21|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=16 new professors at the two Federal Institutes of Technology {{!}} ETH-Board|url=https://www.ethrat.ch/en/medien-medienmitteilungen/16-professorinnen-und-professoren-den-beiden-eth-ernannt|access-date=2020-12-21|website=www.ethrat.ch}}</ref>

== Career ==
Nazeeruddin received a PhD in [[chemistry]] from the [[Osmania University]] in [[Hyderabad]], [[India]]. He served as a lecturer at [[Osmania University]] for two years. He then joined the [[Central Salt and Marine Chemicals Research Institute]] in [[Bhavnagar]], [[India]]. In 1987 he joined EPFL, first as a postdoctoral fellow, and then held several positions as research fellow for seven years. In 2012, he was promoted to "Maître d' Enseignement et de Recherche" (senior lecturer). Since 2014 he has served as full professor at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]] (École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne) and head of the Laboratory for Molecular Engineering of Functional Materials at School of Basic Sciences based at EPFL's Valais campus.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" />

2023 –2029    Professor and Director for the Institute of Perovskite Photovoltaics and Integrated 
	Optoelectronics, IC, Southeast University, Wuxi, China.

2022 –2029	Emeritus Professor, Faculty of Basic Sciences, ISIC, EPFL, Switzerland.

2012 –2022    Professor, Faculty of Basic Sciences, ISIC, Group for Molecular Engineering of Functional 
	Materials, EPFL, Switzerland.

2009–2014 	World Class University Professor, Department of Advanced Materials Chemistry, Korea University (Sejong Campus), Korea.

2014-2019	Brain Korea Plus (BKPLUS 21), Department of Advanced Materials Chemistry, Korea University.

2014-2023	Visiting Professor, King Abdul-Aziz University, Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

2024-2029 	Professor, Imam Abdulrahman Bin Faisal University, Dammam, Saudi Arabia.

2023-2029	Research Fellow, INTI, International University, Malaysia.

2014-2021	      Participated in the Program of Introducing Talents of Discipline to University ("111" Program) Supported by the Ministry of Education of China, North China Electric Power University.

2024-2026	Guest Professor in Haixi Institutes, [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]].

2023-2029      Advisory Board member of the University of Sharjah- College of Sciences 

2024-2026	International Iberian Nanotechnology Laboratory Scientific Advisory Board.

He has also had several affiliated while working and employed at EPFL, such as World Class University Professor (2009–2014) and BKPLUS 21 (2014–2019) at the Department of Advanced Materials, Chemistry of the [[Korea University]], and visiting professor at [[King Abdulaziz University]] in [[Jeddah]], [[Saudi Arabia]] (2014–2023) and at the [[North China Electric Power University]] (2014–2021), and an eminent professor at [[Brunei]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mohammad Khaja Nazeeruddin – 2018 6th International Renewable and Sustainable Energy Conference|url=https://med-space.org/irsec18/mohammad-khaja-nazeeruddin/|access-date=2020-12-23|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Universiti Brunei Darussalam|url=https://ubd.edu.bn/index.php?id=88|access-date=2020-12-23|website=ubd.edu.bn|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Cho|first1=Kyung Taek|last2=Rakstys|first2=Kasparas|last3=Cavazzini|first3=Marco|last4=Orlandi|first4=Simonetta|last5=Pozzi|first5=Gianluca|last6=Nazeeruddin|first6=Mohammad Khaja|date=2016-12-01|title=Perovskite Solar Cells Employing Molecularly Engineered Zn(II) Phthalocyanines as Hole-transporting Materials|url=http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S221128551630372X|journal=Nano Energy|language=en|volume=30|pages=853–857|doi=10.1016/j.nanoen.2016.09.008|bibcode=2016NEne...30..853C |issn=2211-2855|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

== Research ==
Nazeeruddin's research focuses on chemical engineering of functional materials for photovoltaic and light-emitting applications such as [[Perovskite solar cell|Perovskite]] and [[dye-sensitized solar cell]]s, and [[light-emitting diode]]s.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Research|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/gmf/research/|access-date=2020-12-23|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref>

His team conducts research in the area of inorganic chemistry of ruthenium sensitizers that convert solar energy through the use of high surface area nanocrystalline mesoscopic films of oxide semiconductors. These tailored-sensitizers have attracted additional research in dye-sensitized solar cell research. They have synthesized several ruthenium sensitizers (N3, N719 and N749),<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Pizzoli|first1=Giuliano|last2=Lobello|first2=Maria Grazia|last3=Carlotti|first3=Benedetta|last4=Elisei|first4=Fausto|last5=Nazeeruddin|first5=Mohammad K.|last6=Vitillaro|first6=Giuseppe|last7=Angelis|first7=Filippo De|date=2012-09-11|title=Acid–base properties of the N3 ruthenium(II) solar cell sensitizer: a combined experimental and computational analysis|url=https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlelanding/2012/dt/c2dt31340e|journal=Dalton Transactions|language=en|volume=41|issue=38|pages=11841–11848|doi=10.1039/C2DT31340E|pmid=22911010|issn=1477-9234}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=De Angelis|first1=Filippo|last2=Fantacci|first2=Simona|last3=Mosconi|first3=Edoardo|last4=Nazeeruddin|first4=Mohammad K.|last5=Grätzel|first5=Michael|date=2011-05-05|title=Absorption Spectra and Excited State Energy Levels of the N719 Dye on TiO2 in Dye-Sensitized Solar Cell Models|journal=The Journal of Physical Chemistry C|volume=115|issue=17|pages=8825–8831|doi=10.1021/jp111949a|issn=1932-7447 |url=http://infoscience.epfl.ch/record/166677 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Liu|first1=Shih-Hung|last2=Fu|first2=Hungshin|last3=Cheng|first3=Yi-Ming|last4=Wu|first4=Kuan-Lin|last5=Ho|first5=Shu-Te|last6=Chi|first6=Yun|last7=Chou|first7=Pi-Tai|date=2012-08-09|title=Theoretical Study of N749 Dyes Anchoring on the (TiO2)28 Surface in DSSCs and Their Electronic Absorption Properties|journal=The Journal of Physical Chemistry C|volume=116|issue=31|pages=16338–16345|doi=10.1021/jp3006074|issn=1932-7447}}</ref> donor-π-bridge-acceptor porphyrin sensitizers,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Mathew|first1=Simon|last2=Yella|first2=Aswani|last3=Gao|first3=Peng|last4=Humphry-Baker|first4=Robin|last5=Curchod|first5=Basile F. His laboratory is located at the EPFL-Sion Energy center, focusing on organic, inorganic lead halide perovskite solar cells and Light Emitting Diodes research. His laboratory has fabricated blue, green, and red PLEDs with unprecedentedly high external quantum efficiency. His group has investigated solutions (one-step and sequential deposition) and sublimation-deposited perovskite solar cells and obtained a power conversion efficiency of 25%. His group has developed a Perovskite Solar Cells Module (area 26.02 cm2) with an efficiency of 22.4%. == Publications and awards ==
Nazeeruddin is a co-author on numerous peer-reviewed papers and book chapters, and is a co-inventor on many patents.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mohammad Khaja Nazeeruddin Inventions, Patents and Patent Applications - Justia Patents Search|url=https://patents.justia.com/inventor/mohammad-khaja-nazeeruddin|access-date=2020-12-23|website=patents.justia.com}}</ref> According to [[Thomson Reuters]] he has been named a "Highly Cited Researcher" in chemistry, materials science and engineering in 2016 and 2017, and was included in the list of "World's Most Influential Scientific Minds" from all scientific domains.<ref>{{Cite press release|agency=Thomson Reuters IP & Science|title=Thomson Reuters Announces the World's Most Influential Scientific Minds|url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/thomson-reuters-announces-the-worlds-most-influential-scientific-minds-300204299.html|access-date=2020-12-23|website=www.prnewswire.com|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Highly Cited Researchers 2018 - Clarivate Analytics|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/329387365|access-date=2020-12-23|website=ResearchGate|language=en}}</ref> As stated in the ISI listing, he is one of the most cited chemists with more than 196,000 citations and an h-index of 190.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Highly Cited Researchers (h>190) according to their Google Scholar Citations public profiles {{!}} Ranking Web of Universities: Webometrics ranks 30000 institutions|url=http://www.webometrics.info/en/hlargerthan100|access-date=2020-12-23|website=www.webometrics.info}}</ref> His group has earned worldwide recognition and leadership in [[Perovskite solar cell]]s. ''The Times Higher Education'' named him among "the top 10 researchers in the world working on the high impact perovskite materials and devices".<ref>{{Cite web|date=2018-02-06|title=Top universities and researchers in perovskite solar cell research|url=https://www.timeshighereducation.com/data-bites/top-universities-and-researchers-perovskite-solar-cell-research|access-date=2020-12-23|website=Times Higher Education (THE)|language=en}}</ref> Nazeeruddin was included as one of the Top 2% Most-Cited Scientists in the world on the list published by [[Stanford University]] in October 2022.

He is an elected member of the [[European Academy of Sciences]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=European Academy of Sciences - Mohammad K. Nazeeruddin|url=https://www.eurasc.org/user/600/mohammad-k-nazeeruddin|access-date=2020-12-23|website=www.eurasc.org}}</ref> and a fellow of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]].<ref>{{Cite news|last=Testa|first=Andrea|date=2017-03-17|title=Md. Khaja Nazeeruddin elected RSC fellow and EURASC member|url=https://actu.epfl.ch/news/md-khaja-nazeeruddin-elected-rsc-fellow-and-eurasc/|language=en |website=EPFL}}</ref> Fellow of Telangana Academy of Sciences, and Member of the Swiss Chemical Society.  He was awarded the 34th Khwarizmi International Award in Basic Sciences, 2021.

Since 2018 he has been a jury member of the Rei Jaume I foundation in Spain.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Sumatuweb|title=Jurado Protección del Medio Ambiente 2018|url=https://www.fprj.es/es/proteccion-del-medio-ambiente/mohammad-nazeeruddin|access-date=2020-12-23|website=www.fprj.es|language=es}}</ref>

He is the recipient of the best paper award from the journal ''[[Inorganics (journal)|Inorganics]]'',<ref>{{Cite web|title=Inorganics|url=https://www.mdpi.com/journal/inorganics/awards.pdf/0/pdf_167_2018_2_award.pdf|access-date=2020-12-28|website=www.mdpi.com|language=en}}</ref> the EPFL Excellence Prize (1998 and 2006), the [[Mustafa Prize]] (2025) the Brazilian [[São Paulo Research Foundation|FAPESP]] fellowship award (1999), the Japanese Government Science & Technology Agency Fellowship (1998), and Government of India National Scholar award (1987-1989).<ref>{{Cite web|title=EPFL|url=http://nanomatcell.icfo.eu/epfl|access-date=2020-12-23|website=nanomatcell.icfo.eu}}</ref>

He is editor in chief of ''Chemistry of Inorganic Materials'', an advisory board member at ''[[Advanced Functional Materials]]'',<ref>{{Cite web|title=Advanced Functional Materials|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/16163028/homepage/2126_edbd.html|access-date=2020-12-23|website=Wiley Online Library|doi=10.1002/(ISSN)1616-3028|language=en}}</ref> an associated editor at ''Energy Chem'',<ref>{{Cite web|title=Professor Mohammad Khaja Nazeeruddin|url=https://www.journals.elsevier.com/energychem/editorial-board/professor-mohammad-khaja-nazeeruddin|access-date=2020-12-23|website=www.journals.elsevier.com}}</ref> an editorial advisory board member at ''[[Scientific Reports]]'',<ref>{{Cite web|title=Editors {{!}} Scientific Reports|url=https://www.nature.com/srep/about/editors|access-date=2020-12-23|website=www.nature.com|language=en}}</ref> an editorial advisory board member at ''RRL Solar'',<ref>{{Cite web|title=Solar RRL|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/2367198x/homepage/2772_edbd.html|access-date=2020-12-23|website=Wiley Online Library|doi=10.1002/(ISSN)2367-198X|language=en}}</ref> and an editorial advisory board member at ''Artificial Photosynthesis''.
